stories.title: Berrypicking remains the standard for search
stories.summary: Information scientist Marcia Bates argued in 1989 that effective searching requires gathering and revising as you go. Her research on berrypicking techniques suggests that real search processes wander and change shape. Much of what modern product teams are discovering about AI search was documented before the web existed.

stories.title: Apple updates iOS 26 with Liquid Glass
stories.summary: Apple introduced Liquid Glass in iOS 26, a material that automatically updates app appearances when developers recompile with the new SDK. The company stated that apps get this new look immediately. Apps that drew their own custom controls, however, received no such update from the system.

stories.title: Accessibility in immersive LLM chat
stories.summary: As LLM chat patterns spread across the web, developers are being urged to prioritize accessibility to prevent the loss of utility and opportunity for users. The full piece is for subscribers, detailing how to build these immersive experiences without excluding people who rely on assistive technologies.

stories.title: The debate over stochastic parrots
stories.summary: Linguist Emily Bender describes large language models as stochastic parrots, machines that string words together by probability without understanding meaning. The Computer History Museum and IEEE Spectrum recently debated whether these models comprehend their own output or are simply predicting the next word in a sequence.

stories.title: Managing the team search engine
stories.summary: Design team leads often become the primary point of contact for every internal question. While some management literature labels these dependable individuals as rock stars, the constant influx of small queries remains a common operational challenge for those who know where the information lives.

stories.title: Skills as the apps of the agentic era
stories.summary: Skills for AI agents are increasingly written in markdown rather than code. While many function as simple sets of instructions, some developers are beginning to treat them like shippable apps. These skills essentially serve two users, the human typing the command and the agent executing it.

stories.title: The evolution of digital minimalism
stories.summary: Digital minimalism follows the principles of physical minimalism, focusing on doing more with less. While the author notes that physical possessions can sometimes offer self-sovereignty, the practice remains a response to the challenges of the 2000s and 2010s. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Blinkit introduces fees for non-emergency ambulance use
stories.summary: Blinkit will charge Rs 2,500 for non-emergency ambulance transfers to manage a growing volume of routine hospital visits. Founder Deepinder Goyal stated the fee aligns with private ambulance rates and will support the Eternal Foundation. Emergency transfers will remain free as always.

stories.title: CERT-In flags vulnerabilities in Tata Motors apps
stories.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team identified high-severity vulnerabilities in Tata Motors' iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev applications. These flaws could allow unauthorized access to vehicle services and sensitive user credentials. The warnings affect specific versions of apps used by both electric and internal combustion engine vehicle owners.

stories.title: Superior Type releases Heaven typeface
stories.summary: Superior Type has released Heaven, a brutalist grotesque font characterized by round shapes. The design features geometric forms that are intentionally oversized for their allotted space. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: A font that visualizes tokens
stories.summary: Tokenizer Mono is a font that uses modern font witchcraft to highlight token boundaries as you type. Unlike standard tools that pass text through a tokenizer to retrieve data, this font attempts to visualize the process in the browser without performing actual tokenization.

stories.title: The Ramayana as a typeface
stories.summary: Designer Ishan Khosla is exploring how to represent the Ramayana through typography. His work investigates the historical relationship between pictures and words, drawing inspiration from medieval manuscripts that turned opening letters into miniature worlds. The project is part of The Typecraft Initiative.

stories.title: GridType Vol. 1 features stencil typefaces
stories.summary: Slanted Publishers has released GridType Vol. 1, a collection that pairs editorial design with ten stencil typefaces. The volume features an open-spine binding and is presented on an uncoated cover.

stories.title: MLB introduces five-font identity
stories.summary: Major League Baseball has introduced a new five-font identity. The full details regarding the design inspiration and the rollout of these typefaces are currently unavailable due to access restrictions. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Mother Design creates identity for Purple Garden
stories.summary: Mother Design has developed a new visual language for the psychic reading platform Purple Garden. The branding incorporates a living glyph, growing type, and a dawn-inspired color palette. The project reportedly began with a séance.

stories.title: Modern CSS resets for typography
stories.summary: New CSS features like text-wrap: pretty and container query units allow for more precise control over typography. A new stylesheet, tidy-typography.css, gathers these experimental rules to manage vertical rhythm and fluid sizing. Users are advised to apply these features as guardrails rather than blind inclusions.

stories.title: Nubank updates brand foundations
stories.summary: Nubank has updated its brand and digital systems to manage the complexity of serving 140 million customers. The new system aims to fight complexity while maintaining the company's original goal of making finance feel effortless. The design focuses on simple rules for infinite possibilities.

stories.title: Montreux Jazz Festival unveils 2027 poster
stories.summary: The Montreux Jazz Festival has collaborated with illustrator Malika Favre and sculptor Kumkum Fernando for its 2027 poster. This marks only the second time the festival has united two contemporary artists for a design, following a 1987 collaboration between Andy Warhol and Keith Haring.

stories.title: OpenAI updates its image engine with GIF generation and precision markup
stories.summary: OpenAI has launched Images 2.6, adding animated GIF creation and frame-level editing tools to its visual suite. The update promises generation speeds up to 50 percent faster than its predecessor. Users can now circle specific areas of an image to guide modifications. Motion is now a feature.

stories.title: Airbnb plans AI travel agent for 2027
stories.summary: Airbnb will launch an AI-native trip-planning agent in the first half of 2027, according to its Q3 earnings letter. The company claims its experience matching hosts and guests gives it an edge over existing chatbots. It noted that planning a trip on Airbnb is different.

stories.title: Airbnb sets 2027 launch for AI travel agent
stories.summary: Airbnb confirmed its AI travel agent will launch in the first half of 2027. CEO Brian Chesky previously suggested that standard chatbots are not the right interface for travel, as users enjoy the planning process. The company is building a richer interface to accommodate this preference.

stories.title: Perplexity introduces always-on AI teammates
stories.summary: Perplexity has launched Teammates, work-focused AI agents that run 24/7. The tools integrate with Perplexity Computer to deploy agents on user devices for ongoing tasks. The company says the agents build on top of its existing systems to collaborate on large-scale work.

stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber for security testing
stories.summary: OpenAI has unveiled GPT-6 Cyber, a model trained to find vulnerabilities, develop exploits, and suggest patches. In tests, the model reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel and developed exploits for 948 of them. It is five times more effective than its predecessor at finding flaws.

stories.title: Meta adds voice mode to Muse AI
stories.summary: Meta has introduced real-time voice conversations for its Muse AI agent. The update includes expressive avatars that animate in sync with the agent's speech. Users can adjust the voice tone through settings or by asking the agent directly. The feature is available on the iOS app.

stories.summary: Figma has increased the number of AI credits provided to Professional, Organization, and Enterprise plans at no additional cost. This effectively halves the price per credit for Professional users. The company reported a $52.8 million increase in hosting costs during its third quarter.

stories.title: Figma shares drop following AI credit shift
stories.summary: Figma shares fell 7 percent after the company announced it would provide up to 2x more AI credits for the same price. The finance chief stated the company is trading off near-term revenue to invest in its customer base. The credit increase began on 25 August.

stories.title: Figma shifts to in-house AI models
stories.summary: Figma is moving to a proprietary AI model to reduce latency and lower service delivery costs. CFO Praveer Melwani stated the company has already doubled the proportion of tasks powered by its own model. The shift aims to protect operating margins by cutting out third-party AI providers.

stories.title: NID Ahmedabad and Somnath Trust partner on visitor experience
stories.summary: The National Institute of Design and the Shree Somnath Trust have signed an agreement to develop interactive exhibits and wayfinding systems at the Somnath Temple. The collaboration aims to enhance the site through design-led initiatives, including immersive spatial experiences and research into the region’s traditional crafts and architecture.

stories.title: Adobe launches free tool programme for early-stage startups
stories.summary: Adobe has introduced a programme offering startups founded within the last five years free access to its AI-powered creative and marketing tools for 12 months. The initiative includes search analytics from Semrush and is limited to companies that have raised less than $15 million in total funding.

stories.title: Dhee Coding Lab addresses technical training gap
stories.summary: Dhee Coding Lab, founded in 2024, provides technical training to help engineering graduates transition into the technology workforce. The organisation focuses on practical programming experience and recruitment preparation, aiming to bridge the gap between academic learning and the requirements of the IT industry.

stories.title: Delhi-NCR startups cut agency retainers for Canva AI
stories.summary: Startups in Gurugram and Noida are replacing external design agencies with Canva’s enterprise software to reduce operational burn rates. Founders are bringing branding and marketing collateral in-house to accelerate time-to-market. The shift follows a broader corporate mandate for operational efficiency in the final quarter of 2026.

stories.title: Chennai companies hire for vibe coding roles
stories.summary: Companies in Chennai are recruiting developers for AI-assisted software development, a trend described as vibe coding. The role involves using tools like ChatGPT and Cursor to convert natural-language instructions into functional applications. The practice is creating new opportunities for developers who prefer AI-powered prototyping over manual coding.

stories.title: Humble Robotics raises $51 million for autonomous freight
stories.summary: Humble Robotics has raised $51 million in Series A funding to develop its autonomous electric trucks. Led by Obvious Ventures, the round brings the startup’s total funding to $75 million less than a year after its founding. The company plans to build a broader family of autonomous vehicles.

stories.summary: The European Union is launching a platform to support chip design companies, which currently account for less than 1% of global revenue in the sector. The initiative provides access to design tools and manufacturing capacity, aiming to increase Europe’s share of global chip production to 20% by 2030.

stories.title: Aina releases $399 AI ring with joystick and screen
stories.summary: Hardware startup Aina has launched a smart ring featuring a screen, a microphone and a joystick. The device is designed to act as a controller for AI agents and other applications. The company previously produced a three-key controller for Mac users to manage meeting settings and app functions.

stories.title: Cosmoserve raises $6 million for satellite servicing
stories.summary: Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Cosmoserve has raised $6 million in a seed round to support satellite servicing and space debris recovery. The company has opened a new facility, Base 1, to design and operate systems for orbital rendezvous. Total funding for the startup now exceeds $9 million.

stories.title: Startup offers $1 million for materials science AI solutions
stories.summary: Discovered Materials, a San Francisco startup, has announced a challenge for AI models to solve five problems in materials science. The company aims to identify substances for advanced chip manufacturing. Co-founder Advaith Sridhar noted that specifying problems in the field remains more difficult than in mathematics.

stories.title: Brava Security raises $15 million to test AI threat detection
stories.summary: Cybersecurity startup Brava Security has emerged from stealth with $15 million in seed funding. The company offers a platform designed to identify weaknesses in corporate AI-driven threat detection systems. It has already secured customers among Fortune 100 firms in the energy, retail and hospitality sectors.

stories.summary: Canva is laying off 1,271 employees, representing 22 percent of its workforce, as part of a major restructuring. stories.summary: Canva CEO Melanie Perkins is being praised for her communication and support during the company's recent layoffs. The package includes six months of salary, career support, and startup grants. While layoffs usually trigger criticism, the company's exit strategy has been noted for its focus on employee support.

stories.summary: Canva is laying off 1,271 employees as part of an organisational restructuring. The company is offering six months of salary, healthcare, and company laptops to those leaving.
